outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: Minor phrasing like calling “local time” a “timezone indicator,” or not providing an actual timezone name when Slack only shows “local time,” would be minor if everything else were correct.

Critical issues: (1) The agent did not deliver the main required deliverable: a grouped list of up to 12 relevant members. The predicted output reports only one person, while screenshots show multiple accessible relevant people in the directory (e.g., Dalin Stone – Forward Deployed Engineer; Nikola Radisic – Senior Solutions Engineer; Marijan Cipcic – Principal Events Manager; plus support search results including CJ O/Chris jacob as IT Support Specialist). (2) The agent misreported Slack-visible information: it attributes the title/role “IT Support Specialist” to Kristin Sproat, but screenshots show that title belongs to CJ O / Chris jacob, while Kristin’s profile panel shows Away + “3:01 PM local time” and does not visibly show “IT Support Specialist.” This is an accuracy error, not a formatting nit. (3) The agent claimed it could not provide any supporting public message references because none were visible, yet workspace search screenshots show public message threads with clear channel context and timestamps (e.g., in #daytona-support with Nikola (Daytona) and Gabriel Zaccak). Even if those messages weren’t about Kristin specifically, the task required using search to find message references for members when available; the environment clearly supported that, but the output provides none.

Outcome assessment: The agent did use the People directory and did use workspace search, and it avoided DMs/edits, which satisfies the safety/navigation constraints. However, it failed the core task outcome: it neither identified/report up to 12 members nor grouped them, and it included at least one incorrect/misattributed Slack-visible field while omitting available public message references. From an average user’s perspective, they would not have the requested member directory output and could not act on the result.
outcome.primary_intent: Identify (up to 12) Slack-accessible members in the workspace who are associated with software development, support, product feedback, community organization, or documentation, and report only Slack-visible details for each (name, title/role, location/timezone if present, expertise signals, plus a supporting public message reference when available), grouped by likely expertise area without messaging anyone or modifying Slack content. A reasonable user would be flexible on getting fewer than 12 only if the agent clearly explains an external limitation; they would not be flexible on missing the list/grouping entirely, inventing/incorrectly attributing profile fields, or failing to provide message references when they are available via Slack search.
